headline: Hiring a Flooring Replacement Contractor: Signs Your Project Needs a Pro
articleBody:
Swapping out old floors seems straightforward until you pull back the first board and find unexpected structural issues. Knowing when to hire a licensed general contractor can save you thousands in damaged materials and stalled timelines.

Signs It Is Time to Call a Professional:
- Soft or uneven subflooring: If your floor bounces, dips, or shows water staining, the subfloor must be leveled or replaced before new planks go down.
- Tricky stairs and transitions: Stair treads, landings, and varied heights between tiled kitchens and hardwood halls demand precise cuts and structural anchoring.
- Glued or site-finished materials: Adhesives and poured finishes carry strict open-time and curing demands that leave zero margin for error.
- Gas appliance disconnections: Moving stoves or water heaters requires a qualified technician to disconnect lines safely before flooring work begins.
- Heavy furniture logistics: Large cabinetry, islands, or grand pianos complicate clearing and reinstalling work areas.

When Professional Guidance Helps:
A proper installation requires an accurate moisture evaluation, structural subfloor repairs, and exact trim heights.
